title: RDS (Relational Database Service)
body: An AWS managed database service that handles database administration tasks like provisioning, patching, and backups. Supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, and SQL Server with automatic failover and read replicas.

title: DynamoDB
body: A fully managed NoSQL database service that provides fast and predictable performance with seamless scalability. Supports key-value and document data models with automatic sharding and replication across multiple availability zones.

title: Redshift
body: AWS's data warehouse service designed for fast analytical queries on large datasets. Uses columnar storage and parallel query execution; optimized for OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) workloads, not transactional systems.

title: IAM (Identity and Access Management)
body: An AWS service for managing user access and permissions. Allows creation of users, groups, roles, and policies to control who can access which AWS resources and what actions they can perform.

title: CloudWatch
body: An AWS monitoring and observability service for collecting metrics, logs, and alarms from AWS resources and applications. Enables tracking of resource utilization, application performance, and operational health.

title: SNS (Simple Notification Service)
body: A fully managed pub/sub messaging service for sending notifications (SMS, email, HTTP) and distributing messages to multiple subscribers. Decouples applications and enables asynchronous communication.

title: SQS (Simple Queue Service)
body: A fully managed message queue service that decouples producer and consumer applications. Enables asynchronous processing, load leveling, and reliable message delivery with automatic retry and dead-letter queues.

title: AWS Well-Architected Framework
body: A set of best practices and design principles for AWS architectures across five pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, and Cost Optimization. Guides design decisions and reviews.

title: Availability Zone (AZ)
body: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within an AWS Region. Applications can be distributed across multiple AZs for high availability and disaster recovery.

title: Region
body: A geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones. AWS has regions worldwide; applications should be deployed across multiple regions for compliance and disaster recovery. Each region is independent.
